title: Covered-Case Instrument Return
instruction: Three opaque cases stand side by side in one row. Use the left arm to grasp each lid's central handle, lift it and slide it horizontally to the left of that case, clear of the right wrist camera's view. The right arm holds the incoming module and uses its wrist camera to check each opened case. If occupied, move the right arm away and replace that lid before checking another case. Case inspection order is unrestricted. Place the module only in a visually confirmed empty case, move the right arm clear, and replace its lid. Keep stored modules undisturbed and leave all three lids seated on their matching cases.
context: At a shared measurement station, a robot returns one interchangeable instrument module to protected storage. It must inspect three opaque cases, preserve the two modules already stored, choose the vacant case, and reseat every lid. This tests a routine workplace return workflow in which a wrong destination disrupts later retrieval.

The case and lid shells use a polypropylene-like rigid-plastic contact analogue (static/dynamic friction 0.35/0.25, zero restitution); the central handle uses a high-grip contact material (1.2/1.0, zero restitution). The unmarked 80 g instrument modules are rigid cubes using the station's object contact material.
scoring: End score, not best-ever score. A violation observed at a 20 Hz control step latches score 0: the incoming module leaves the workspace, or the incoming module enters an initially occupied case by at least 10 mm in both horizontal directions and 3 mm below the cavity top (including stacking on the stored module); it also gives 0 if a stored module is wholly expelled beyond its own cradle plus 5 mm, a lid is discarded, a mechanism loses integrity, or a task solid penetrates another by more than 3 mm. Case-opening order is unrestricted. Otherwise 0.25 when any case is physically open for 0.20 s; 0.50 when any two distinct cases have each been physically open for 0.20 s; 0.75 when the incoming 40 mm cube is fully placed and released in the originally empty case, with all eight corners inside the 50 mm interior to 1.5 mm, its bottom supported within 2 mm and its orientation within 10 degrees of an equivalent aligned pose. Full score 1.0 requires both stored modules still correctly supported, all three lids released and seated on their matching physical case rims, and the incoming placement stable for 1 s with no violation and success termination within 2,400 steps. Released means both gripper collision-hull bounds are at least 8 mm from the incoming module, and any gripper within 60 mm is open at least 45 mm; stable means module speed relative to cradle at most 15 mm/s and angular speed at most 0.1 rad/s. A timeout is capped at 0.75. Before these milestones, the score is 0. Right-wrist RGB and actions can be inspected in the saved trial; visual understanding is not scored separately. The scoring and geometry code defines the exact predicates.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps at 20 Hz (120 s of simulation).
reset_notes: A reset restores all objects, arms and scorer state to the fixed layout. No consumables.
fidelity: Three 75 g removable rigid lids have central handles and underside grooves. The 80 g modules and shells use simplified cuboid collision geometry. Gravity, contact, friction and grasping run in PhysX with unmodified YAM arms and cameras. Dimensions and materials are representative; no real-hardware calibration, contact-force measurement or continuous-collision proof has been performed. Scoring observes the state at 20 Hz; a brief forbidden crossing between control steps may be missed.
